tasks.title: Rate cap of an outgoing topic
tasks.statement: In `dds_topics.yaml` a topic has `rate_limit: {r}.`. The PX4 1.17 uXRCE-DDS client calls `orb_set_interval` with a period of 1000/`rate_limit` ms converted to whole milliseconds. What is the maximum rate at which the topic goes out to ROS 2, in Hz?
tasks.solution: Period = (uint64)(1000/r) ms, the fractional part is dropped, rate = 1000/period. For example, 30 Hz → 33 ms → 30.30 Hz; 60 Hz → 16 ms → 62.5 Hz. Without `rate_limit` the period is 10 ms, so no more than 100 Hz.

tasks.title: How long a stall Offboard survives
tasks.statement: A node publishes `OffboardControlMode` at **{f} Hz**, `COM_OF_LOSS_T = {lt} s`. What is the longest node stall (a pause on top of the normal period) that PX4 still does not treat as signal loss, in s?
tasks.solution: The signal is lost when the last message's timestamp is older than `COM_OF_LOSS_T` (offboardCheck.cpp). The gap between messages = the period 1/f + the stall d; the condition d + 1/f < L → d < L − 1/f. At 2 Hz and 1 s the margin is only 0.5 s.

tasks.title: UART load from the DDS bridge
tasks.statement: `uxrce_dds_client status` shows `Payload tx: {p} B/s` on TELEM2 at **{b} baud** (8N1). What share of the line capacity does the traffic take, in %?
tasks.solution: An 8N1 byte is 10 bits, capacity = baud/10 bytes/s. Share = P/(B/10)·100 %. `Payload tx` counts only the CDR data, without the XRCE headers and framing (at most ~23 bytes per sample), so the course guideline is to keep it below ~50 % (with headers that is about 70 % of the line).
